chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Bint Ilyas, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"When he reaches his maturity at thirteen years old and enters the fourteenth, the obligations that fall upon those who have reached puberty fall upon him, whether he has had a wet dream or not. Bad deeds are recorded against him and good deeds are recorded for him, and everything is valid for him, except if he is a spendthrift or weak-minded."

key_terms.الْمُحْتَلِمِينَ: those who have had a wet dream (sign of puberty)

ai.seo_question: What is the age of legal maturity for boys in Shia Islam and what are the conditions?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes thirteen lunar years as the definitive age of *bulugh* (legal maturity) for boys, emphasizing that religious accountability (*taklif*) and the recording of deeds commence at this threshold regardless of physical signs of puberty like *ihtilam*. It further clarifies that full legal capacity is granted unless the individual is classified as *safiha* (a spendthrift) or *da'eef* (weak-minded), a distinction crucial for understanding inheritance and financial transactions in Shia jurisprudence.
